items.title: How do I pick a renderer? What does each one do?
items.description:
Pick the renderer under Settings → Video Settings → Renderer (only changeable while the game is not running):

• Zink: translates the game's OpenGL onto the system Vulkan stack (GL→Vulkan→Metal). Best for MC 26.x and modded setups; chunk loading stays smoother.
• MobileGlues: an OpenGL→Metal translation layer with broad compatibility, good for lightweight setups and older versions. Per-frame translation cost while chunks load is high (Android devices behave the same way — a known trait).
• LTW: a lightweight OpenGL 3.3→ES translation layer (same lineage as the Android one). Low overhead, good for 1.21.x and earlier lightweight versions. MC 26.x is not supported (see the next entry).
• Krypton Wrapper (<=26.2, formerly NG-GL4ES): the gl4es used by ZalithLauncher 2; shaders go through a glslang+SPIRV-Cross pipeline, and upstream claims almost every MC version runs (old versions through 26.x); it replaces VGPU -- if you hit corrupted textures or broken atlases on legacy versions, switch here first;
• gl4es(≤26.2): ZalithLauncher 2's traditional gl4es (PojavLauncherTeam branch, built from source); a pure-C lightweight string-rewriting shader converter with no extra shader pipeline; coexists with Krypton Wrapper as fallback options -- the second legacy-version fallback (holy gl4es was removed this round; this renderer takes its place);
• MoltenVK: a standalone renderer that maps the Vulkan API directly onto Metal. On MC 26.2+ you can pair it by switching to the Vulkan backend in the in-game Video Settings → Graphics (with the framerate unlock it can exceed the display refresh rate). It and Zink are two independent options — Zink uses the system Vulkan stack, which is not the same as "selecting the MoltenVK renderer".
• Auto: the launcher picks automatically based on the game version.

Rule of thumb: new versions / modpacks → Zink; older versions → Krypton Wrapper first, then try gl4es(≤26.2) (MobileGlues / LTW for lightweight play); choose MoltenVK when you want the Vulkan backend.

items.title: LTW crashes immediately on MC 26.x?
items.description:
Known capability boundary — the launcher has a built-in pre-check (starting 26.x with LTW pops a notice and blocks the launch, so you don't waste a trip).

Why: LTW on iOS translates desktop OpenGL 3.3 on top of Apple's system GLES 3.0 backend, while MC 26.x's cloud rendering pipeline needs "texture buffers" (samplerBuffer, a core desktop-GL feature since 3.1). The ES 3.0 backend simply cannot provide it, so the cloud shader always fails to compile and the game crashes at the title screen (log signature: 'samplerBuffer: Illegal use of reserved word' + 'Failed to load required shader programs: pipeline/flat_clouds').

Fix: switch Settings → Video Settings → Renderer to Zink or MobileGlues (both fully support 26.x — Zink provides desktop-class GL 4.x, MobileGlues ships a texture-buffer emulation layer).

LTW's sweet spot: 1.21.x and earlier keep working as usual. Backporting a texture-buffer emulation into LTW is structural work; it is on the roadmap (following the same path MobileGlues' emulation layer took).

items.title: What is Krypton Wrapper (formerly NG-GL4ES)? How does it relate to VGPU and gl4es?
Is MobileGlues stuttering while chunks load normal?
How do I use FSR upscaling? Which renderers support it?
Can MetalFX Temporal replace FSR?
items.description:
Short answer: the temporal version is not possible today — it's a hard engine-level dependency, not the launcher being lazy.

[Why not]
MetalFX's temporal mode requires the game to supply, every frame: a per-pixel motion-vector buffer (mandatory in the API), a depth buffer, and camera jitter/reprojection matrices. Vanilla Minecraft's render pipeline produces no motion vectors — producing them would need a "velocity pass" added inside the game's renderer, an engine/mod-level change (on the order of Sodium/Iris-scale work). The launcher's presentation bridge only ever sees the finished frame — it has neither the depth nor the camera data of any frame, so correct motion vectors cannot be conjured. Forcing pure temporal accumulation would produce severe ghosting, and Apple's API flat-out requires the input.

[What about the spatial version?]
MetalFX spatial is, like FSR 1.0, single-frame upscaling with the same image-quality class. Wiring it up would need an iOS 16+/A13+ device floor plus an extra texture interop layer — marginal gain, so it's not adopted for now.

[Current advice]
For framerate: use FSR Ultra Quality/Quality (Zink or MobileGlues). For image quality: turn FSR off and render native. If upstream (the Sodium family or Mojang) ever produces motion vectors, temporal upscaling will be re-evaluated on the launcher side.

items.title: Can Arm ASR (Arm Accuracy Super Resolution) replace FSR?
items.description:
Short answer: not adopting it for now. Unlike MetalFX temporal, Arm ASR has no hard motion-vector dependency (like FSR 1.0 it is single-frame spatial upscaling — it was in fact derived and tuned from FSR1). The blockers sit at both the implementation shape and the payoff:

[Why it doesn't plug in]
Arm ASR's official implementation is a Vulkan/DX12 compute shader, while Zink — going through the system Vulkan stack — caps the game's OpenGL at 4.1, which lacks the compute shaders that only 4.3 brings. The reference implementation cannot run as-is; porting it means rewriting the algorithm as fragment shaders (exactly what the launcher did for its built-in FSR).

[Why the payoff is small]
Arm ASR's performance selling point is compute-shader tiling and shared-memory access tuned for Mali GPUs (Arm's own). Run through a fragment pipeline on an Apple GPU, all of that evaporates, and the remaining quality delta versus FSR1 is tiny (both are FSR1-derived algorithms).

[Current advice]
The most practical framerate win on Zink is simply using FSR: the latest build completed Zink's GLSL 4.1 adaptation (automatic version downgrade + half-precision packed-function completion). If a native Vulkan/Metal presentation path (with compute shaders) ever lands, ASR and MetalFX spatial will be re-evaluated.

items.title: What alternatives to FSR 1.0 exist? Why was it chosen in the end?
items.description:
Within the single-frame spatial-upscaling class, the candidates and verdicts (2024–2025 public reviews and source research):

[NVIDIA NIS (Image Scaling)] Open source (MIT), single-pass upscale+sharpen combined, cross-platform (works on AMD/Intel too). Public comparisons rate its quality equal to FSR 1 — nearly identical; single-pass is in theory lighter on bandwidth. This is the only same-class alternative worth future consideration — adoption would take one round of GLSL version adaptation (the same workload as the FSR adaptation we already completed).

[Qualcomm GSR (Game Super Resolution)] Open source (BSD-3), single-pass spatial upscale. Its selling point is wave-occupancy tuning for Adreno GPUs — on Apple GPUs all of that falls flat, and its quality is same-class FSR1-derived. No benefit in switching.

[Apple MetalFX spatial] Digital Foundry's measured quality on the Resident Evil Mac port was worse than FSR 1 (same engine, both spatial), and adoption needs iOS 16+/A13+ plus an extra texture interop layer.

[Anime4K / FSRCNNX and other video-lineage algorithms] Edge reconstruction aimed at anime content; benefits on general 3D scenes are inconsistent and the compute cost is higher — unsuitable for real-time full-screen game upscaling.

[The temporal family (DLSS / FSR 2–3 / XeSS / MetalFX temporal / Arm ASR)] The quality ceiling is genuinely one tier higher, but every member depends on engine-produced motion vectors / depth / jitter sequences — the launcher side cannot conjure them. See the previous two entries on Arm ASR and MetalFX.

Verdict: FSR 1's EASU is already first-tier quality in the single-frame spatial class (some measurements beat MetalFX spatial), and we've already completed its GL 4.1 adaptation on Zink; switching to any same-class algorithm yields less than the risk of one more adaptation. The real quality leap arrives when temporal inputs become available.

items.title: How do I adjust the framerate cap / VSync?
The picture looks blurry / soft. What can I do?
Can I install shaders (Iris/OptiFine) and performance mods? Any traps?
On a 1.20.x modpack + Zink + FSR, the game picture shrinks into the bottom-left corner (large blank areas elsewhere)?
items.description:
Typical picture: with Zink selected and an FSR tier enabled, the game enters and plays fine, but the image occupies only the bottom-left two-thirds of the screen with the rest blank.

Mechanism: with FSR on, the game renders at low resolution (screen ÷ tier factor) into the bottom-left of a full-size buffer, and an upscale pass then magnifies it to fill the screen. On 26.3 this chain is verified fine; on some 1.20.x packs (BMC2 etc.) the upscale result never reaches the final readback buffer that goes on-screen, so the raw low-res frame is presented directly = the shrunken corner.

Fixed by the launcher (Task99 detection + Task100 authoritative present + Task103 ground-truth loop + Task104 far-corner sentinel + Task105 viewport adaptation): on-screen output no longer depends on the driver's glFinish readback — every frame the launcher itself reads the authoritative image straight from the framebuffer and presents independently. Sentinel verification was upgraded to two corners (Task104): the bottom-left sentinel can only prove "upscaled fragments exist in that corner", not full-coverage; the opposite-corner sentinel (top-right) is where full-frame rasterization must pass — both sentinels hit = the upscale truly landed full-frame; either one missing = the game's original image is immediately handed to CoreAnimation to stretch full-screen (bilinear stretch, geometry always full). Task105 went further: the upscale input region no longer assumes the launcher-told window size but reads the game's actual presentation viewport every frame (MC 1.20.1's final present draw conveniently sets it right before) and follows it — when some pack's mod-size chain shrinks the actual presented region, the upscale simply magnifies the real region; geometry stays full-screen. How to verify: search the log for "[OSMBridge] Task103 EASU sentinel verdict" — LANDED means both sentinels hit and EASU covered the full frame; NOT LANDED means the stretch fallback engaged (picture instantly full-screen); far=N/M is the far-corner hit rate; the "[OSMBridge] Task105 viewport evidence" line shows the game's real presentation viewport vs the launcher-told size (DIVERGED = adaptive takeover engaged); the "[OSMBridge] Task104 EASU viewport check" line shows the viewport size the driver actually holds.

Interim self-help if you don't want to wait for the update: set Settings → Video Settings → FSR 1.0 Upscaling to "Off" (the picture renders at native full resolution; framerate drops accordingly).

items.title: How do I type in-game (chat, commands, naming)? What's the difference between the two keyboard buttons?
Joystick does nothing / movement requires holding Shift?
items.description:
These were systematically fixed in newer builds (virtual-key state direct-write + keybind-profile auto-correction + joystick heartbeat re-send) — normally a push just moves.

If you still hit it:
1. Check Settings → Controls → Default control scheme — is it "custom" (a custom layout)?
2. Check whether in-game Key Binds got mangled (restore defaults);
3. Update to the latest build and retry — older builds had incomplete input fixes.

items.title: Any notes on Bluetooth mice / gamepads?
How do I edit the custom control layout? How do I recover a broken one?
items.description:
Editing: open the in-game menu → Keybind Editor (or pick "custom" under Settings → Controls → Default control scheme then edit) — drag, scale, add buttons/drawers/joysticks, then save as a new layout.

Recovery: the editor has "Restore default controls" — the factory layout is deleted and rebuilt (your other custom layouts are untouched). If a corrupted layout file leaves you with zero controls in-game, the launcher automatically falls back to the default layout to keep the game playable.

Tip: the factory custom layout ships a full "keyboard icon" drawer (the key panel) with all the common keys; "Restore default controls" also picks up the latest factory version with corrected binds.

items.title: Keyboard closes after every character in the multiplayer menu? (closed as upstream)
items.description:
Symptom: in the multiplayer address field the keyboard dismisses after each typed character.

Verdict: upstream Minecraft behavior -- the 26.x multiplayer screen tears down and rebuilds its text-input context after every character (a Stop->Start cycle whose interval exceeds any launcher-side debounce window). The launcher ships two mitigations (typing-aware adaptive debounce + the auto-open-keyboard switch honoring every request), but the upstream rebuild flash cannot be fully eliminated; FCL/Zalith show the same. Closed as an upstream issue; it will disappear when Mojang fixes the text-context management.

Workaround: tap the input-method button (pencil icon) to reopen the keyboard and keep typing, or paste the address from elsewhere.

items.title: How should I allocate memory?
What do the launcher's memory-related entitlements do?
items.description:
• Increased memory limit: lets iOS grant the launcher more memory — typically raises the cap by ~15%. Obtainable via "sideloading signatures" (SideStore/NB Helper etc.) or a paid Apple Developer certificate (see BV1regH6RETM for a guide).
• Extended virtual memory: lets iOS give the launcher more address space — combined with the former, typically another ~15% of cap. Only available with a paid developer certificate (see BV1regH6RETM).

items.title: Installing a modpack says "missing parent version JSON / json not found"?
How do I install mods? Crashes / incompatibility after installing?
Which Java does each MC version need?
Where is the launcher's data (saves, mods, layouts) kept? How do I back it up?
Downloading versions/assets is slow or failing?
Blocks, entities, or clouds show see-through / punched-through artifacts?
items.description:
This is usually a compatibility issue between the Sodium mod's "improved transparency" option and the renderer — not a broken launcher or world.

Fix: in-game, open Video Settings → Sodium → find "Improve transparency" (translucency sorting) and turn it off; the artifacts disappear.

This issue is renderer-independent — it can happen on both Zink and MobileGlues; toggling the option off is enough.

items.title: Green / garbled screen regions after enabling FSR (especially on Zink)?
items.description:
Fixed (in two rounds). Cause: Zink goes through the system Vulkan stack, whose shader language (GLSL) caps at 4.1, while the FSR upscale shader declares 4.5. In old builds the compile failure fell into a downgrade path, but the downgrade never actually told the game to "go back to full-resolution rendering" — so only the bottom-left region of the picture was being rendered and the rest showed uninitialized VRAM content (the green/garbled blocks).

The fix took two rounds:
1. Round one: automatic shader-version adaptation to Zink's GLSL ceiling + a true fallback to full-resolution rendering when upscaling is unavailable (no more green screen);
2. Round two: completed the half-precision packed functions missing in 4.1 and corrected a shader type constant — upscaling on Zink now works natively (no downgrade needed).

If you still see green regions: upload latestlog.txt (the log shows which path was taken).

items.title: After switching to the background and back, the game freezes / blacks out / drops frames abnormally?
How do I report a crash or black screen?
Generic self-help steps for "stuck on some screen / spinning forever / instant crash"?
A huge modpack (hundreds of mods) gets stuck on the loading screen on first launch?
Modpack crashes a few seconds after launch; the log says the LWJGL version is incompatible?
items.description:
Typical picture: not a hang but a fast exit (within seconds), identical on every renderer. Searching latestlog.txt for "LWJGL version is not compatible" shows:

Installed version: 3.4.1
Required version: 3.3.1

This is Sodium's pre-launch safety check: it demands the LWJGL version matching that Minecraft version (1.20.1 pairs with 3.3.1, 26.x with 3.4.1) and refuses to start otherwise. Old launcher builds hardcoded 3.4.1 to let 26.x through, which got 1.20.1 packs (like BMC2) rejected by Sodium 0.5.13.

Fixed by the launcher (dynamic reporting): at launch it reads the matching LWJGL version from the game's version metadata and reports that to Sodium — each version reports its own. To verify: search the log for "[Tools] LWJGL report version"; it should show the version-matched value (1.20.1 → 3.3.1).

If you still hit this: confirm you're on the latest build (Settings → About, check the Commit), then attach latestlog.txt.

items.title: Modpack crashes mid-launch; the log says "Could not execute entrypoint stage"?
Modpack crashes deep into launch; the log mentions paintings or sparsestructures errors (listFiles NPE / FileAlreadyExistsException)?
items.description:
Typical picture: all mods loaded, launch progresses ~30–40 seconds (window init, resource loading) then exits; renderers don't matter. Search the log for either signature:

1. NullPointerException + Arrays.stream + PaintingPackReader.scanPacks (the paintings mod);
2. FileAlreadyExistsException: config/sparsestructures.json5 (the sparsestructures mod).

This is neither a broken mod nor a missing file — it was an environment defect in older launcher builds: Java has two relative-path resolutions — java.io.File uses the process working directory, java.nio uses user.dir — and the old launcher only set the latter. The two resolvers each looked in a different place: paintings checked "resource-pack folder exists" with one and listed the directory with the other (listing a location that doesn't exist → NPE); sparsestructures decided "config absent" then created it and landed on a same-named file in the real directory (→ already-exists). The same pack never double-standards on desktop (a desktop launcher's working directory is always the game dir), so both mods are fine there.

Fixed by the launcher (Task97): before the JVM starts, the process working directory is aligned to the game directory — identical to desktop. To verify: search the log for [CwdAlign] Task97; there should be a "process CWD aligned to game dir: ..." line, and the previously ever-present "Cannot access RandomAccessFile logs/latest.log" error also disappears (the game's own log now writes into the instance's logs/ properly).

If you still see the above after updating: confirm you're on a build at or past the Task97 fix commit (Settings → About → Commit), then attach latestlog.txt.

items.title: A 26.x Fabric/NeoForge modpack crashes seconds after launch; the log says "Loading library SDL" or can't find org/lwjgl/sdl/SDL?
items.description:
Typical picture: the pack (mostly performance packs with Sodium/Iris) prints its mod list, enters the vanilla bootstrap phase, then exits suddenly; renderers don't matter. Log signatures:

1. "Description: Loading library SDL" + "java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: org/lwjgl/sdl/SDL";
2. Slightly earlier, a "Failed to get system info for SDL Platform" (same-family precursor, safe to ignore).

Cause: since MC 26.3, windowing and input moved from GLFW to SDL3, requiring LWJGL's SDL bindings (the lwjgl-sdl module, only present in the launcher's 3.4.1 set). The old launcher's version-based LWJGL picker only understood vanilla-shaped version ids ("26.3"), not the pack-shaped prefixed ones ("fabric-loader-0.19.5-26.3-e4ecd7db"), and picked the 3.3.3 set — no SDL bindings inside — so the fifth library load (SDL) inevitably crashed. Unrelated to renderer, memory, or Sodium itself (Sodium's version check had already passed by then).

Fixed by the launcher (Task98): version extraction now uses prefix-agnostic anchored parsing; Fabric/NeoForge/Forge-shaped 26.x all correctly select 3.4.1. To verify: search the log for "Using LWJGL 341"; the line above should read "[LWJGLSel] Task98: MC major 26 extracted from version id ..."; SDL then loads and the Loading library SDL crash is gone.

On an old build: just update the launcher. Interim workaround: in Settings → the instance's edit page, manually set the LWJGL version to 3.4.1.

items.title: MC 26.3 release crashes mid-launch; the crash report says "Initializing game" with MacosUtil or NSApplication in the stack?
items.description:
Typical picture: on 26.3 release (packs included) the mods finish loading, the main window is up, and right as the game is about to start it exits. Log signature:

"java.lang.NoSuchMethodException: Method cannot be found for signature ..." + stack ca.weblite.objc.Client.sendProxy → MacosUtil.disableCloseWindowMenuItem → Window.<init>, Description: Initializing game.

Cause: the launcher spoofs macOS to run LWJGL/JNA on iOS; MC 26.3 release takes it at face value and, during window init, calls into macOS-only AppKit menu integration (disabling the "Close window" menu item — via NSApplication/NSMenu classes that only exist on macOS). iOS only has UIKit, so the class lookup fails and it crashes. Unrelated to renderer, Sodium, or memory (26.3-rc-3 and earlier lacked this call, which is why the same launcher didn't crash before).

Fixed by the launcher (two layers, Task99 + Task100): before the JVM starts, three minimal stub classes (NSApplication/NSMenu/NSMenuItem) are registered in the Objective-C runtime. After the first fix, 26.3 proceeds to a second layer — if the crash report says "NullPointerException ... because "windowsMenu" is null" (same MacosUtil/Initializing game), the stub lacked the windowsMenu outlet; Task100 completed the family (windowsMenu/appleMenu/helpMenu/servicesMenu). To verify: search the log for "[AppKitStub] Task99: NSApplication/NSMenu/NSMenuItem stubs installed" and "[AppKitStub] Task100: windowsMenu requested"; if you see an "unexpected selector" line, please report it with latestlog.txt (26.3+ calling a new menu API means the stubs need extending).

On an old build: just update the launcher; no in-game settings need changing.

items.title: A 26.3 pack crashes the instant you enter a save/world; the log reports a sodium pipeline compile failure, "preprocessor directive cannot be preceded by another token"?
items.description:
Typical picture: the main menu is fine; the crash hits the moment you enter a save and the world loads. The crash report's Description is "Render Frame"; the direct cause is "Failed to find or load pipeline sodium:pipeline/solid_terrain".

Mechanism: the 26.x render frontend compiles GLSL to SPIR-V uniformly, and Sodium's terrain shaders #include shared snippets (globals/fog/chunk_vertex). All three snippet files shipped by Sodium verifiably lack a trailing newline — the launcher's #include expander spliced the line-number restoration directive (#line) directly onto the last meaningful character, producing invalid GLSL (exactly the preprocessor-directive error in the log). Vanilla snippets all end properly, so in the same session hundreds of vanilla shaders compiled fine and the first Sodium shader exploded — which is also why this is unrelated to renderer, memory, or LWJGL.

Fixed by the launcher (Task103): the expander now guarantees the output ends with a newline before splicing #line — gluing is impossible; vanilla shaders are unaffected (they already ended properly, so no newline is added). To verify: search the log for "[amethyst-include] expanded" — Sodium shaders (e.g. sodium:blocks/block_layer_opaque) expand with no GLSL parse error following, and entering worlds works.

Interim workaround on old builds: remove Sodium / Sodium Extra / Reese's Sodium Options from the pack (terrain rendering falls back to the vanilla pipeline; framerate drops).

items.title: Modpack crashes when creating a new world (no crash report; the log just stops)?
items.description:
Typical picture: menu/title screens fine; after tapping "Create New World" the screen freezes or crashes outright; latestlog.txt ends abruptly (no exit, no crash stack, no hs_err). Common last lines involve spark's "Starting background profiler..." or "[Amethyst] Patching ...libasyncProfiler.so.tmp".

Mechanism: the spark profiler, when a server first starts (creating/entering a world), unpacks its bundled native library libasyncProfiler into config/spark/tmp and loads it. That library is built for macOS and carries a code signature — after the launcher rewrites its platform tag to iOS, the signature hashes no longer match and the system loader kills the process outright (a silent crash that cannot be caught). This is the "re-tagging a signed library is always fatal" rule: unsigned libraries survive re-tagging; signed ones never do.

Fixed by the launcher (Task106 dual-layer + Task107 correction): (1) the library load is intercepted — spark detects the failure and automatically falls back to its pure-Java sampler (profiling still works; the game continues); (2) generic protection — after platform re-tagging, an ad-hoc signature is rebuilt (page hashes recomputed; Task107: the earlier "neutralize to unsigned" approach proved to break JNA — the system loader rejects unsigned libraries outright with a missing-code-signature error; signed libraries are fatal when re-tagged but load fine after re-signing). To verify: search the log for "[Amethyst] Task106: blocked dlopen" (interception active) or "[Amethyst] Task107: re-signed" (re-signing active) — once present, world creation proceeds. Interim workaround on old builds: remove spark from the pack.

If it still crashes and the last line isn't spark-related: mind memory — world creation is the memory peak phase (a 537-mod pack measured 5.1GB before creation); when device memory runs dry the system also kills silently. Consider lowering the launcher's max memory or render distance.

items.title: The Metal (metallum) renderer crashes in-game. What now?
items.description:
If the game crashes in-session after switching video settings or reloading resources (crash stack inside AGXMetalConverter / the AGX driver layer), this is a known issue of the Metal renderer (metallum backend) on some system versions — unfixed upstream as well; the launcher cannot work around it.

Interim: Settings → Video → Renderer — switch back to ANGLE, gl4es, or MobileGlues and keep playing (saves and mods are unaffected by renderer switches).

The issue where the launch screen required manually tapping "Cancel launch" has been fixed (the Metal first-frame signal is wired up; the overlay dismisses itself when the picture arrives).

items.title: A Forge modpack crashes on launch (IForgeVertexFormat / OptiFine errors)?
items.description:
When the log shows java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: net.minecraftforge...IForgeVertexFormat or OptiFine-related reflection failures, the pack's bundled OptiFine is binary-incompatible with that Forge version (interface signature drift) — a mod-side problem.

Fix: remove OptiFine from the mods folder (or swap in a build matching that Forge version) and relaunch. When the launcher detects Forge + OptiFine coexisting it prints a warning anchor in the log ([PojavLauncher] Task202: OptiFine detected alongside Forge) for quick confirmation.

Also: if Forge 26.x pops a "missing software!" tiny file dialogs prompt at launch (asking whether to open the early-display-errors page), that's the fallback error dialog after Forge's progress window failed to initialize — iOS has no desktop dialog components, and the console y/n read auto-skips on EOF, so it never deadlocks. The latest build disables the Forge progress window by default (it failed to initialize on translation layers anyway); after updating, the prompt no longer appears.
